symptom_spec.intended_behavior: A derived embedding table's catalog key_column records the ORIGIN column its _row_id values actually came from, so a reader can follow the provenance by joining source.<key_column> = derived._row_id. key_column is provenance only — the physical key of every embedding table is invariantly _row_id (jammi-db/src/store/mod.rs::EmbeddingTableSpec, ::materialize_embedding_table), and _row_id holds the source key's values.
symptom_spec.observable: propagate_embeddings and materialize_context recorded the literal key_column="_row_id" instead of the source's origin column. Over a source keyed by a real column (e.g. paper_id) with NO _row_id column, propagate -> the derived table records Some("_row_id") not Some("paper_id"). The catalog auto-resolvers then interpolate that name into a scan of the RAW source: filter_keys_by_split and hydrate_value_columns (jammi-ai/src/pipeline/context_set.rs) issue SELECT arrow_cast("_row_id",'Utf8') FROM <raw source> and fail 'Schema error: No field named _row_id'. Reached end-to-end by train_context_predictor, which builds ContextRequest::new(..) with embedding_table: None (defaulting to auto-resolution) plus split + value_columns, so it resolves whichever table is newest — a propagated one — and cannot scan its own origin.
symptom_spec.control: EXACT equality on the derived record's key_column (never != "_row_id", which passes vacuously on None, on "", and on any wrong-but-different name). A POSITIVE control asserting the origin fixture truly has no _row_id column, so the RED is attributable to the false provenance and not an unrelated missing column. A NEGATIVE control asserting a source whose origin key genuinely IS _row_id still records Some("_row_id") — failing any fix that blanket-drops or blanket-substitutes the literal. Resolution pinned against the record the producer RETURNS (resolve_embedding_table orders on app-supplied wall-clock created_at and can tie); the one deliberate shadowing case asserts the resolution landed on the propagated table so a tie fails loudly.

which_gate_missed: write-side provenance was recorded but never asserted — no test read back a derived table's catalog key_column. Every existing fixture (jammi-ai it/bench/gpu_capability, jammi-server) was itself _row_id-keyed, so a hardcoded "_row_id" was indistinguishable from a correct inherit: the two agree on every fixture in the repo. The defect was unobservable until a non-_row_id-keyed origin ran the propagate -> auto-resolve -> split/hydrate path end to end.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: A jammi-cli integration test spawns its server on a port no other process can take, so the CLI's connect succeeds regardless of what else runs concurrently. The harness either holds the port until the server binds it, or lets the server bind an ephemeral port and reports back the one it got.
symptom_spec.observable: crates/jammi-cli/tests/it/server_harness.rs::free_port binds 127.0.0.1:0, reads local_addr().port(), then DROPS the listener and returns a bare u16 — releasing the port before the server binds it. Under the parallel workspace suite (cargo test --workspace runs many test binaries concurrently) another process can take the port in that window, and the CLI then fails: 'Error: Configuration error: connect to jammi endpoint: transport error'. Observed on cargo test --workspace --exclude jammi-python at channels::cli_channels_add_column_rejects_retype (flight port 40421); the same test passes in isolation (15/15) and on a re-run of the full suite, so it is load-dependent, not deterministic. Aggravated by wait_ready polling only the HEALTH port while the failure surfaced on the FLIGHT port — readiness is asserted on a different port than the one the client uses.
symptom_spec.control: A test that makes the race deterministic rather than probabilistic: hold a listener on the port between free_port and the server's bind (or spawn N harnesses concurrently under load) and assert the server still comes up — failing on the current release-then-rebind shape. A fix that only widens wait_ready's timeout must NOT pass: the failure is a stolen port, not a slow start.

which_gate_missed: no gate — the harness's own doc comment ACKNOWLEDGES the race and argues it away ('There is a small race between release and the server's bind, but on a CI host the kernel does not immediately re-hand the same port, so this is reliable for a test harness'), which is exactly the CLAUDE.md band-aid tell-sign 'a comment justifying why a wrong primitive is fine here'. The flake is load-dependent and self-clearing on retry, so it reads as infrastructure noise rather than a defect and no gate ever attributes it.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: Every catalog key_column names a column of the source it points at, so a reader that follows the provenance (source.<key_column> = derived._row_id) can always resolve it. Where the engine cannot establish that at the write site, it should not leave the caller to discover it as a raw planner error from an unrelated verb much later.
symptom_spec.observable: ENGINE GAP, not caller error: import_embeddings offers key_column as a REQUIRED parameter, records it verbatim as the source-side provenance its own readers later scan, cannot validate it at that site, and does not warn. crates/jammi-ai/src/pipeline/import.rs::ImportPipeline::run enforces only non-emptiness and passes Some(key_column) to materialize_computed_embedding_table, which delegates to materialize_embedding_table and registers ResultTableKind::Model (crates/jammi-db/src/store/mod.rs); resolve_embedding_table filters kind = 'model' (crates/jammi-db/src/catalog/result_repo.rs), so the imported table IS auto-resolved, and filter_keys_by_split (crates/jammi-ai/src/pipeline/context_set.rs:490) / hydrate_value_columns (:545) interpolate the recorded name into SELECT arrow_cast("<name>",'Utf8') FROM <raw source>. This is the same false-provenance class as esc-025 reached through a public verb. It differs from esc-025 in DECIDABILITY, not in blame: propagate_embeddings held the source record's key_column at the call site and wrote the literal "_row_id" anyway (ground truth in hand, substituted), whereas at the import site source_id is a label stamped on a catalog row rather than a resolvable relation, so no ground truth is obtainable there.
symptom_spec.control: MUST FAIL TODAY (empirically verified, not asserted). Register a source keyed by doc_id with a split column and NO column named nope. import_embeddings(source_id="papers", key_column="nope", ...) -> the write SUCCEEDS: observed Ok((status "ready", key_column Some("nope"))). Then a reader that follows the provenance -- assemble_context with split = Some("split = 'train'") -- hard-fails with a raw planner error: observed Other("Context split: scan: Schema error: No field named nope. Valid fields are papers.public.src.doc_id, papers.public.src.split."). Passing shape for a fix: the failure is a typed provenance-mismatch error naming the table, the recorded key_column, and the source, instead of a raw DataFusion 'No field named nope'. A fix must NOT be accepted on a control that only asserts the write is rejected -- see the tenant-iso collision below.

which_gate_missed: no gate covers a write-side provenance value that is only decidable on the read side. The write site cannot check it (see the tenant-iso collision) and the read sites that CAN check it treat the mismatch as an ordinary planner failure rather than a provenance defect, so the recorded lie is never attributed to the verb that recorded it. esc-025 closed the two sites where the ground truth WAS in hand at the call site; this row is the residual where it is not.

The oracle states the premise VERBATIM at crates/jammi-server/tests/it/tenant_isolation_oracle.rs:1518-1523: 'import_embeddings writes a ready embedding table from precomputed vectors, stamping the catalog row with the scoped tenant. (a) HEAVIER -- require a registered source for import and re-derive the tenant oracle's isolation argument, since import would then resolve a tenant-scoped relation at write time; this changes what the oracle proves and is a design decision, not a fix.
